precepts.text: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man. That tells you what the thing of Ecclesiastes 1:9 is.
precepts.point: There is no remembrance of former things. Why? Because the spirits from the past return to the future.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is the thing? Solomon tells you in chapter 6: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.” The thing is man on earth.

So “that which is done is that which shall be done”: whether man keeps the commandments or does not keep the commandments. “and there is no new thing under the sun.” From the time of Genesis, as it has been is going to be so in these last days. There are no new incidents on this earth; the things done by man are the things that were done in the past. And “There is no remembrance of former things”, because the spirits from the past return to the future.

Paul says the same in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Written for our learning today, because the things done in the past reoccur. In a Christian mind everything is new; but nothing is new. To deal with these reoccurring events, we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors.

Ezra shows it too: “I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is a circle, “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” It is a continual event that reoccurs over and over. And the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets”, comparing one thing to another.

That is why what we read in Daniel 3, Nebuchadnezzar setting up his golden image, is coming to pass again with the Trump administration and the golden statue the pastors prayed over. The man that hath been is the man that shall be.

precepts.text: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.
precepts.point: The thing that hath been is that which shall be, and there is no new thing under the sun. Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? It hath been already of old time, which was before us: before our generation, it was in the past. And there is no remembrance of former things.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Solomon says it again in chapter 3: “That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.”

It is the same as “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. One generation comes and another goes; the old die and the young are born. The sun has its cycle, the wind has its circuits, and the rivers run into the sea and return again. Generations have their circuits and cycles the same way.

So what is to be has already been. Before our generation it was already in the past, only “There is no remembrance of former things”. That is why a man can stand in a moment and feel, I remember this.

What is the thing that hath been? Solomon names it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. So he explains it himself: the thing that have been is man.

Just like the wind, the sun, the moon and the rivers have a flow, likewise man: we come and we go. You and I have been here before, in different cycles of life. That is why it is called deja vu, a French term that literally means already seen: the sensation of having already experienced a situation even though you know it is happening for the first time.

Already seen, because you are already meant to be there. The prophets saw things that came to pass. When the prophets saw us going on slave ships, we had to live out what they saw. So when John saw America in flames, we have to live out what John already saw. We are catching up to the prophecies, and what leads up to them is already set in motion. You can't change it.

precepts.point: The thing that hath been is that which shall be, and there is no new thing under the sun. Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing?” The wise man knows the interpretation of the thing. And “a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine”.

The thing that hath been, in Ecclesiastes 1, is talking about man. Man has been around before, but “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.” It takes wisdom to interpret that thing.

So the wise man understands the cycle: the generations pass and come again, and what the prophets already saw is what we are living out now. The wise man knows it is man that hath been, and that is why there is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.text: Solomon said, I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. That means all kind of sin. I'm showing you when Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.
precepts.point: Ahijah caught the new garment that was on Jeroboam and rent it in 12 pieces. Imagine you got a new garment on and somebody just start ripping pieces off. What the hell is this? Take thee ten pieces: I'm going to give you 10 tribes. That's the northern kingdom. But he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel”. What happened? Solomon got old. He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he built houses of worship for their individual gods. They did not all serve the same god: Chemosh, Remphan, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of those gods required child sacrifice; some involved sexual orgies. And Israel had to pay taxes for those gods.

Solomon said it himself: “And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.” Madness and folly means all kind of sin. However your mind can go, Solomon went there. When Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee”, but “Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.” That is why Ahijah tore Jeroboam’s new garment into twelve pieces and told him to take ten: the northern kingdom, while one tribe was kept for David’s sake. That is the tabernacle of David that fell.

precepts.text: There is no remembrance of former things: David will not remember who he is, and neither do you.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
If David is alive in these last days, “David their king, whom I will raise up unto them”, why doesn't anyone know it? Solomon says: “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.”

David will not remember who he is, and neither do you. Our minds are wiped, everybody. We don't know who's who. That is why it says love your neighbour as you love yourself: you don't know who is who.

And that is a good thing. In the old school we used to say, oh, this one's David, and that caused a lot of partiality and a lot of problems. Don't do that. Don't try to guess who anybody is either. Little brother calling himself Samson: you don't know, brother. Just stop it. The Lord will raise up David; it is not ours to name him.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
“And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad”. We saw persecution against our brothers in France; it hasn't gotten here yet, and they say America is the major hub. When it happens, can you stand the rain? That's why we say don't take the convocations lightly.

People read these things and say, oh, that's old time. But Solomon says: “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” That's you and me. We read Maccabees and Acts 8:1 and say that could never happen again? You're simple as hell. What happened in 1 Maccabees 1 and Daniel 3 is what Revelation 13 speaks of, no buying and selling, and it leads to death.

Paul said the same thing: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Those old-time things were written for us to learn from, because they are going to happen again. We need patience and the comfort of the scriptures because we are going to go through what our ancestors went through: how did they deal with it, how did they survive?

Herod killed James and, because it pleased them, took Peter also. And Trump joked about bringing back public executions. The Christians don't understand what is about to come; in here we understand, because what has been is what shall be.

“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” What was done in Egypt is what shall be done. The Most High hardened Pharaoh's heart and the hearts of his servants so they would not let Israel go; he will harden the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom the same way.

That is why the captivities repeat their patterns, and why this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon and of the Greeks. These things must come to pass; there is no new thing under the sun.
